newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends up on fund buying, soyoil down.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends up on fund buying, soyoil down.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures settled higher Monday on a late round of commodity fund buying and soyoil futures settled slightly lower.
"We saw a little bit of fund buying in thin trade, so the market just went up," said one soymeal pit trader.
In late soymeal trade, Rosenthal Collins bought 300 lots March, and Smith Barney, E.D. and F. Man and Merrill Lynch each bought 100 lots March.
Trade in both pits was subdued for most of the session. Cash soyoil and export markets have been very quiet because of various world holidays, traders said.
China is celebrating the Lunar New Year, Brazil is celebrating carnival, and the Malaysian palm oil markets are also closed for holidays.
Monday's main feature was spread trade, floor sources said. Cargill was buying soyoil and selling soymeal, and Iowa Grain was taking the other side of the trade, a floor source said.
CBOT soymeal ended up $0.90 to $1.80 per ton, with March soymeal up $1.40 at $236.70. Soyoil futures ended down 0.18 to 0.06 cent per pound with March down 0.06 at 23.87 cent per pound.
The soymeal market was also supported somewhat by news that Mexico is forecast to import 331,000 tonnes of duty-free U.S. soymeal in 1997, traders said.

On the day, Iowa Grain and Rosenthal bought 250 lots soymeal and Shatkin, Arbor and Karlov bought 250 lots. In soyoil trading, Chicago Corp bought 200 lots May and R.J. O'Brien sold 100 lots March, traders said.
CBOT soymeal volume was estimated at 11,000 lots, which was below the 12,594 traded on Friday. Soyoil volume was estimated at 7,000 lots, also below the 8,247 traded on Friday.
